item.title: Best AI strategy for your business: Make it Midwest practical, says startup duo reunited after DEG exit
item.description: For many companies racing to adopt artificial intelligence, the biggest challenge isn’t the technology; It’s knowing where to begin, said Neal Sharma, whose new venture alongside Craig Sizemore aims to turn AI hype into real business value.

item.title: Keystone Angels takes wing with emerging leader; next up: saving startups from the valley of death
item.description: A familiar face in Kansas City’s business ecosystem is stepping into a leadership role aimed at tackling one of the biggest challenges facing local startup founders: access to early-stage funding.

item.title: Thai Orchid opening new location in Shawnee’s emerging entertainment district this fall
item.description: It’s time to bring Thai Orchid’s homecooking, well … home, said second-generation owner Jonathan Rojjanasrirat, teasing the October opening of a new Shawnee location for his family-owned, street food-inspired restaurant in a thriving entertainment district.

item.title: Redbud VC drops $25M Fund II in its attempt to ‘out-hustle the market’ for top talent, Midwest unicorns
item.description: A new $25 million fund for Columbia-based Redbud VC is expected to help identify and develop top-tier innovators before they head to the coasts to find more abundant capital, said Brett Calhoun.

item.title: C2FO passes half-trillion-dollar mark as businesses pivot to working capital from traditional debt
item.description: In a high-cost environment, businesses across the globe are prioritizing “on-demand” liquidity over new debt, said Sandy Kemper, announcing Wednesday that Kansas City-based C2FO has now provided more than a half-trillion dollars in working capital to entrepreneurs worldwide.

item.title: Kansas City data centers and AI flip the script on job security
item.description: Construction trades are riding the biggest building boom in decades, in part due to data center projects. But the artificial intelligence that the facilities power could upend the job market for everyone else.

item.title: No late risers: KC’s hottest line leads to a sell-out doughnut; owners balance appetite with days-long production
item.description: Slow Rise is building a loyal following in Kansas City, but the same thing that makes these destination treats so unique — a sourdough twist on the traditional doughnut — brings production challenges. Here's how owners Jessica and Jeff Dunkel are filling the opportunity amid risk.

item.title: The end of gear hunting: Wacka wants to automate-away manual price chasing
item.description: Late nights. Too many browser tabs. Price comparisons across half a dozen retailers. Waiting weeks for the right moment to buy. Justen Wack knows exactly how outdoor gear purchases usually happen, he said — because the tech founder used to grind through the process himself.

item.title: KC-backed (and built) AI startup rebrands amid shift to tackling America’s supply chain pain points
item.description: With its pivot from video transcriptions to bulk inventory tracking, one of Kansas City’s most-promising, emerging tech startups is rebranding to match the new direction, co-founders Warren Wang and Cole Robertson said.

item.title: This brand on the rise smells a lot like cookies fresh out the oven; why Brown Suga tastes better in Leawood
item.description: A fan-favorite Kansas City cookie shop has found its sweet spot in Leawood’s mixed-use Park Place district, said founder Ebony Paul, noting the setting for Brown Suga Bakes’ second storefront clicked right away.
